tool_calls.output:
Knowledge that is NOT in the AFSIM output: the munition type hierarchy (which weapons are air-to-air missiles, precision-guided, cluster munitions, anti-radiation...), the platform type hierarchy (fighters, SAM launchers, engagement radars, command posts...), and the scenario's force structure (chain of command, echelons, nations, coalitions).

REASONING IS ON: the endpoint holds the OWL-RL closure, so types, subclasses, the chain of command, inherited facets, coalitions and platform nations are already inferred - plain triple patterns are enough, no property paths needed.

AFSIM things are individuals. Each AFSIM type string (platforms.type, events.weapon_type) is a bs:SimulationType individual that is an instance of its ontology class and every superclass, and has that class's facets (bs:guidance, bs:warheadType, bs:intendedTarget). Each AFSIM platform is an individual of its platform class. So to find the AFSIM strings for any category, query instances: ?t a bs:SimulationType , <category> ; bs:simTypeName ?name.

Join keys - always put these literals in SQL, never IRI local names:
  bs:simTypeName     == platforms.type, events.weapon_type, weapon_inventory.weapon_type (one class may have several alias strings)
  bs:simPlatformName == platforms.name, events.platform, events.target
  bs:simSideName     == platforms.side (on bs:Coalition individuals)

Force structure: units (bs:MilitaryUnit) have bs:echelon, bs:nation, bs:service and are bs:directlySubordinateTo their parent unit; platforms are bs:assignedTo the one unit that owns them. Both are single steps. bs:subordinateTo is the inferred whole chain: use it for 'platforms or units under a unit at any depth'. Units and platforms carry inferred bs:coalition; platforms carry inferred bs:nation.

tool_calls.name: ontology__ontology_overview
tool_calls.output:
Knowledge that is NOT in the AFSIM output: the munition type hierarchy (which weapons are air-to-air missiles, precision-guided, cluster munitions, anti-radiation...), the platform type hierarchy (fighters, SAM launchers, engagement radars, command posts...), and the scenario's force structure (chain of command, echelons, nations, coalitions).

REASONING IS ON: the endpoint holds the OWL-RL closure, so types, subclasses, the chain of command, inherited facets, coalitions and platform nations are already inferred - plain triple patterns are enough, no property paths needed.

AFSIM things are individuals. Each AFSIM type string (platforms.type, events.weapon_type) is a bs:SimulationType individual that is an instance of its ontology class and every superclass, and has that class's facets (bs:guidance, bs:warheadType, bs:intendedTarget). Each AFSIM platform is an individual of its platform class. So to find the AFSIM strings for any category, query instances: ?t a bs:SimulationType , <category> ; bs:simTypeName ?name.

Join keys - always put these literals in SQL, never IRI local names:
  bs:simTypeName     == platforms.type, events.weapon_type, weapon_inventory.weapon_type (one class may have several alias strings)
  bs:simPlatformName == platforms.name, events.platform, events.target
  bs:simSideName     == platforms.side (on bs:Coalition individuals)

Force structure: units (bs:MilitaryUnit) have bs:echelon, bs:nation, bs:service and are bs:directlySubordinateTo their parent unit; platforms are bs:assignedTo the one unit that owns them. Both are single steps. bs:subordinateTo is the inferred whole chain: use it for 'platforms or units under a unit at any depth'. Units and platforms carry inferred bs:coalition; platforms carry inferred bs:nation.
